redis_version: Redis server v=7.4.2 sha=00000000:1 malloc=jemalloc-5.3.0 bits=64 build=ee01ef89c4d6eeb8

config.topology: primary :7301, replicas :7302/:7303 (replicaof 7301); all limiter nodes share the primary in healthy mode

phases.name: healthy
phases.how_induced: no fault; all nodes on the primary

phases.name: partial_partition_k1
phases.how_induced: client-subset isolation: node 3 pointed at dead address 127.0.0.1:7399; nodes 1-2 keep the live primary

phases.name: full_partition_bounded
phases.how_induced: kill -9 on the primary (7301); replicas hold no write path

phases.name: full_partition_skewed
phases.how_induced: primary still down; 90% of attempts land on node 1, whose local cap binds

phases.name: healed
phases.how_induced: primary restarted from the same data dir (AOF state survives)

phases.name: full_partition_failopen
phases.how_induced: primary killed; fallback policy = fail-open (Envoy failure_mode_deny=false equivalent)

phases.name: full_partition_failclosed
phases.how_induced: primary still down; fallback policy = fail-closed (Envoy failure_mode_deny=true equivalent)

notes: The three limiter nodes are objects in this one harness process (one host clock); multi-host clock skew is out of scope — the bound covers skew analytically at W + 2*delta.
Each phase uses a fresh bucket key, so phases measure rested-bucket behaviour and do not contaminate each other.

In-flight decisions at the instant of kill -9 can be lost either way by TCP semantics; the harness counts a decision only when the limiter returns one (local fallback included), so the kill instant contributes at most a few hundred ms of local-mode decisions, which are inside the bound by construction.
